data.title: Meta Platforms (META) Q3 earnings preview: Can AI returns justify surging infrastructure spending?
data.description:
Referenced assets

Key takeaways

  • Advertising remains Meta’s core earnings engine, but investors increasingly want evidence that AI tools can lift monetisation and justify rapidly rising infrastructure spending.
  • Capex, margins and free cash flow are the key risks, especially if management signals another sizeable increase in AI-related spending heading into 2027.
  • Technically, 653.17 is the key support, while a break above 734.84 may reopen the path towards 777.60/793.70.

Ahead of Wednesday’s 21 Q3 2026 earnings, Meta Platforms (META) faces a critical test of whether its artificial intelligence (AI) investments are generating sufficient returns to justify surging infrastructure spending and maintain its valuation premium.

Meta is scheduled to release its results after the US market closes on Wednesday, 21 October 2026, followed by its earnings conference call at 4:30 pm Eastern Time.

Meta’s shares have retreated by 2.82% since the start of October through 19 October 2026, reflecting broader weakness in AI-related technology stocks, and Meta also underperformed several of its “Magnificent Seven” peers such as Alphabet (+1.76%), Apple (+3.82%), Tesla (+3.94%), Microsoft (+4.04%), and Amazon (+5.73%) (see Fig. 1).

Investors are now increasingly questioning whether rising capital expenditure will translate into sustainable earnings growth. The pullback follows mounting concerns over AI infrastructure financing, with semiconductor stocks also coming under selling pressure.

The street is expecting a 23.6% year-on-year increase in Meta’s Q3 revenue to US$63.34 billion and Q3 earnings per share of US$6.53.

In addition, options markets are pricing in roughly a ±7.1% earnings move, below Meta’s 10-year average peak earnings-day move of ±10.4%, suggesting a smaller-than-normal reaction.

Against this backdrop, Meta’s earnings reaction will likely hinge on advertising revenue growth, AI monetisation, operating margins, 2027 capital expenditure guidance and free cash flow.

Let’s now highlight seven fundamental factors that traders should be watching.

1. Advertising revenue growth: the core earnings driver

Meta’s advertising business, encompassing Facebook, Instagram, Reels and its other platforms, remains the principal source of revenue and cash generation.

Q3 consensus revenue of US$63.34 billion represents approximately 23.6% year-on-year growth, close to the upper end of management’s US$61 billion–US$64 billion guidance range.

Traders will focus on whether AI-powered advertising tools are improving recommendation quality, ad targeting and conversion rates sufficiently to support higher advertising prices and impressions.

2. AI monetisation: can Meta convert investment into revenue?

Meta’s AI monetisation strategy is increasingly important to its valuation, especially following the launch of its Muse AI assistant and continued investment in advertising automation.

Reports indicate that Muse has attracted more than two million daily users, although demonstrating meaningful revenue conversion remains a key challenge.

The market will monitor user adoption, potential subscription or commercialisation models, enterprise demand and the extent to which AI improvements contribute to the existing advertising business.

3. Capital expenditure: the biggest valuation risk

Based on current guidance mentioned in the Q2 2026 earnings results release in July, Meta’s full-year 2026 capital expenditure guidance is US$130 billion–US$145 billion, including finance lease principal payments, an increase in the lower end of the prior guided spending range of US$125-US$145 billion, as it builds out AI computing infrastructure and data-centre capacity.

Importantly, the market is no longer focused solely on whether demand for AI infrastructure remains strong. Investors increasingly want evidence that the returns on these investments can justify their financing and operating costs.

S&P Global has recently highlighted growing concerns over hyperscaler AI-related financing commitments and the sustainability of infrastructure investments.

4. Operating margins and expense growth: profitability under pressure

Meta has guided full-year 2026 operating expenses of US$165 billion–US$169 billion, reflecting higher infrastructure costs, AI-related research and development, and legal expenses.

The critical issue is whether strong advertising revenue can continue to generate sufficient operating leverage to absorb these costs.

Management previously indicated that full-year 2026 operating income should exceed 2025 levels. Traders will assess whether that outlook remains achievable and, more importantly, how much further operating costs could increase in 2027.

5. Free cash flow: sustainability of the AI investment cycle

Free cash flow is emerging as one of the most important indicators of Meta’s financial flexibility.

Despite strong advertising profitability, Meta’s substantial capital expenditure commitments could continue to absorb an increasing share of operating cash flow.

Investors will be looking for signs that operating cash flow growth can eventually outpace infrastructure investment, allowing Meta to maintain its shareholder returns without compromising its AI ambitions.

6. Forward guidance: the most important post-earnings catalyst

Management’s fourth-quarter revenue outlook and preliminary 2027 spending expectations may have a greater influence on share-price performance than the reported Q3 numbers.

Traders will focus on whether advertising demand remains resilient heading into the year-end holiday season and whether Meta can maintain its growth trajectory amid higher infrastructure costs.

7. Market positioning and the broader AI sell-off

Meta’s results arrive at a sensitive juncture for US technology stocks.

The Nasdaq 100 and semiconductor sector have recently experienced significant weakness amid concerns over elevated AI infrastructure spending and the sustainability of the investment cycle.

Share-price implication: A stronger-than-expected earnings release could attract renewed buying interest in Meta and the wider AI-related technology sector. However, disappointing guidance could accelerate selling pressure, particularly if investors view Meta’s spending trajectory as further evidence of weakening returns on AI investment.

Fundamental bottom line: what matters most for traders

The market is increasingly distinguishing between companies benefiting from AI investment and those generating measurable financial returns from it.

For Meta, advertising remains the earnings engine, while AI infrastructure spending is the principal valuation risk.

The most bullish outcome would combine stronger advertising revenue, resilient operating margins and convincing evidence that AI adoption is translating into higher monetisation, without another substantial increase in projected expenditure.

Conversely, even an earnings beat may fail to support the share if management signals accelerating AI costs, weaker free cash flow or limited revenue visibility into 2027.

Let’s now focus on the multi-month outlook of Meta and key levels to watch from a technical analysis perspective

Technical analysis: Positive follow-through after bullish breakout from 13-month descending range

The price action of Meta staged a bullish breakout on 15 September 2026 from a four-week descending range, running from its current all-time high of 796.25, printed on 15 August 2025.

Thereafter, Meta rallied 16.3% to a 12-month high of 777.60 on 24 September 2026, then staged an 11% pullback while holding above its 50-day moving average in October.

The recent multi-month up move from the 30 July 2026 low to the 24 September 2026 high has been accompanied by higher-than-average volume relative to the prior multi-month rally of 21 April 2025 to 15 August 2025, suggesting that the bulls are likely in control (see Fig. 2).

The volatility-adjusted relative strength (VARS) of Meta against the Nasdaq 100 exchange-traded fund (QQQ) has trended upwards since 23 June 2026 and has remained above the centreline since 12 October 2026, a condition for further potential outperformance of Meta over the Nasdaq 100.

Watch the 653.17 key medium-term pivotal support (also the 50-day moving average) to maintain Meta’s potential multi-month uptrend phase. A clearance above 734.84 intermediate resistance (also the 20-day moving average) sees the medium-term resistance zone of 777.60/793.70 in the first step.

However, failure to hold and a daily close below 653.17 negate the bullish tone, suggesting a potential slide towards the key 200-day moving average, which acts as the next support at 626.68; a break below it would expose the major support of 540.90.

data.title: Tesla Ahead of Q3 2026 Earnings: strong deliveries, weakening demand in China, and a major test for Cybercab
data.description:
Referenced assets

  • Tesla beats Q3 delivery expectations: Tesla delivered 486,532 vehicles in the third quarter of 2026, exceeding analyst forecasts by 5.3%. Investors will now focus on profitability, automotive margins, and cash flow when the company reports earnings on October 21.
  • Strong exports offset weakening demand in China: September wholesale sales of China-made Tesla vehicles rose 5% year over year to 95,366 units, driven by a 58% surge in exports. However, domestic sales declined 9%, highlighting persistent competitive and pricing pressures.
  • Cybercab expansion offers growth potential but faces regulatory hurdles: Tesla is rapidly expanding its autonomous vehicle fleet in Texas, with Dallas emerging as a potential next market. However, safety requirements and an October 30 regulatory deadline could influence the pace of commercialization.

Tesla is scheduled to release its financial results for the third quarter of 2026 on October 21, after the close of trading on Wall Street. Investors will assess not only the performance of the company's core automotive business but also its progress in developing autonomous taxis and expanding its energy storage operations. Although September sales of China-made vehicles reached their highest level of the year, growth was driven primarily by exports, while demand in the domestic Chinese market remained under pressure. Meanwhile, Tesla continues to advance its Cybercab project, whose future depends on both technological capabilities and decisions by US regulators.

Tesla beats delivery expectations as investors await financial results

Tesla's upcoming earnings release will be one of the key events of the October reporting season for the US technology and automotive sectors. The company will present its detailed third-quarter financial results on October 21, providing investors with important information on revenue, profitability, and cash flow. Initial figures concerning Tesla's operating performance are already available. According to data released on October 2, the company delivered 486,532 vehicles in the third quarter, exceeding the previous analyst consensus of 461,974 units. This represents a result approximately 5.3% above expectations, although deliveries were still around 2.1% lower than a year earlier. Vehicle production totaled 464,391 units.

Beating delivery expectations is a positive signal, but it does not necessarily indicate an improvement in financial performance. The key question is whether Tesla managed to maintain healthy margins amid intense price competition. Higher vehicle sales do not automatically translate into proportional profit growth, particularly when additional demand is supported by discounts or more attractive financing terms. Investors will also focus on Tesla's ability to generate cash. The company is investing heavily in artificial intelligence, autonomous driving, and robotics, making the financial health of its core automotive operations an important factor in its ability to execute its long-term strategy.

Record september sales in China, but growth depends on exports

The situation in China's electric vehicle market remains an important factor in assessing Tesla ahead of its earnings release. In September, the company's Shanghai factory recorded its highest monthly wholesale sales volume of 2026, including vehicles intended for both domestic customers and export markets. Total sales reached 95,366 vehicles, representing a 5% increase compared with the same period last year. However, the headline improvement masks a significant divergence between domestic sales and exports. Tesla's exports from China increased by 58% year over year in September, reaching 30,529 vehicles. At the same time, domestic sales declined by 9% to 64,837 units. This means that September's wholesale sales growth was driven entirely by increased deliveries to overseas markets.

A similar pattern can be observed in the figures for the first nine months of the year. Total wholesale sales of China-made Tesla vehicles increased by approximately 23% to 743,060 units. Exports surged by more than 108% during this period, while domestic sales declined by nearly 12%. The growing importance of international markets has allowed the Shanghai factory to maintain strong operating volumes despite weakening local demand. Nevertheless, conditions in China's automotive market remain challenging. Tesla faces increasingly intense competition from domestic manufacturers offering a wide range of lower-priced electric vehicles. Reduced government purchase incentives and aggressive pricing strategies across the industry are adding further pressure. Tesla has also relied on discounts to support demand, which may negatively affect profitability.

For investors, the main question is therefore not only whether Tesla can sustain export growth from Shanghai, but also whether higher delivery volumes will translate into stronger financial results. Persistent pricing pressure could limit the benefits of increased vehicle sales.

Long-term forecasts point to higher vehicle sales and energy storage growth

Despite challenges in China, analysts expect Tesla to gradually increase global vehicle sales over the coming years. According to the consensus published by the company on September 29, deliveries are projected to reach approximately 1.77 million vehicles in 2026 and rise to 1.92 million in 2027. Longer-term forecasts suggest that Tesla could exceed 2 million annual deliveries in 2028 and reach around 2.7 million vehicles by 2030. Achieving these targets will require Tesla to maintain the competitiveness of its core models, stabilize demand across major markets, and continue expanding its operations. Increasing competition from both traditional automakers and Chinese electric vehicle manufacturers remains a major challenge.

At the same time, energy storage is becoming an increasingly important part of Tesla's business model. During the third quarter, the company deployed energy storage systems totaling 13.7 GWh, compared with analysts' previous expectations of 15.9 GWh. Although the result fell short of forecasts, the segment's longer-term growth prospects remain promising. According to the September consensus, annual energy storage deployments are expected to reach 56.5 GWh in 2026 and increase to 148.8 GWh by 2030. This would represent more than a doubling of the business over four years.

Growing demand for energy storage, supported by the expansion of renewable energy generation and power infrastructure, could create significant opportunities for Tesla. The segment also plays an important role in diversifying revenue and reducing the company's dependence on electric vehicle sales. Ahead of the upcoming earnings report, investors will focus not only on the pace of expansion in Tesla's energy business but also on its profitability and ability to generate positive cash flow.

Cybercab expansion accelerates as Tesla prepares for the next stage of autonomous mobility

One of the most important pillars of Tesla's long-term strategy remains the development of autonomous transportation. The Cybercab project is intended to enable the company to enter the mobility services market with vehicles that do not require a traditional human driver. For investors, it is a central element of the argument that Tesla should be valued not simply as an automaker, but also as a company developing artificial intelligence-based technologies.

Cybercabs registered in Texas increased from 169 to 319, representing an addition of 150 vehicles. The materials also indicate that the fleet serving Austin has surpassed 300 vehicles, marking an eightfold increase in just 30 days. These figures suggest rapid expansion, although vehicle registrations do not necessarily correspond to the number of vehicles actively providing fully autonomous commercial services. Tesla's operations in Austin could serve as a foundation for expansion into additional US cities. Ashok Elluswamy, Tesla's head of AI software, has suggested that Dallas could become one of the next markets. However, the company has not announced a specific timeline for launching the service there.

Elon Musk has previously emphasized that the expansion of autonomous taxi operations will proceed gradually. Particular attention is being given to challenging driving scenarios, including railway crossings, complex intersections, and situations involving limited visibility. System safety remains one of the fundamental conditions for successful commercialization. For investors, the development of autonomous taxis carries significance beyond fleet expansion alone. The ultimate success of the project will depend on Tesla's ability to establish a service that can be scaled safely and profitably across multiple cities. Consequently, management commentary during the third-quarter earnings presentation regarding expansion plans, operating costs, and technological progress could prove particularly important.

Regulatory challenges could slow cybercab development, with October 30 marking a key deadline

The development of autonomous taxis also presents significant regulatory challenges. US National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) has required Tesla to respond to 21 questions concerning Cybercab safety certification. One of the central issues involves whether a vehicle designed without conventional pedals complies with US safety regulations, particularly those governing braking systems.

Tesla reportedly received an extension until October 30, 2026, to submit its responses, despite requesting additional time until November 20. This means that just nine days after its quarterly earnings release, the company faces another important deadline related to the future of its autonomous vehicles. Regulatory requirements could directly affect the pace of Cybercab commercialization. Even substantial technological progress does not guarantee rapid deployment on a large scale if the vehicle's design and operating systems fail to meet applicable safety standards.

From an investment perspective, the key question is whether Tesla can transition from expanding test fleets and limited deployments to a business model capable of generating recurring revenue. Regulatory delays or required vehicle design modifications could postpone the expected financial benefits.

Tesla shares rebound, but investor sentiment remains cautious

The improvement in September wholesale sales in China generated a positive market reaction. Following the release of the figures, Tesla shares gained as much as 2.05% on Friday. The stock finished the previous week 3.27% higher, reaching $382.70.

However, the short-term rebound does not change the fact that Tesla shares remain under pressure. Stock has declined by approximately 15% since the beginning of 2026, making it the weakest performer among the Magnificent Seven companies. Investor sentiment continues to be influenced by questions about Tesla's ability to deliver on its ambitious technology projects and turn them into profitable businesses. Autonomous driving, artificial intelligence, and robotics could create new revenue streams, but they also require substantial investment.

As a result, the upcoming earnings report will be assessed not only in terms of vehicle sales but also through Tesla's ability to finance future growth without significantly weakening its cash flow. Investors are likely to pay particular attention to management commentary on planned capital expenditures, automotive margins, and the timetable for launching new services. Given the high expectations surrounding autonomous mobility, even strong vehicle delivery figures may not be enough to produce a sustained improvement in sentiment unless Tesla also offers a convincing outlook for profitability.

Tesla Q3 Earnings: what will matter most to investors?

Tesla's financial results on October 21 will provide an opportunity to assess whether the company can translate relatively solid operating performance into stronger financial fundamentals. Vehicle deliveries exceeded analysts' previous expectations, but persistent pricing pressure and declining domestic sales in China remain significant challenges. At the same time, businesses beyond traditional automotive manufacturing are becoming increasingly important to Tesla's investment outlook. Energy storage could gradually account for a larger share of the company's operations, while Cybercab remains a project with substantial potential but also considerable technological and regulatory uncertainty.

The most important question for investors will therefore be whether Tesla's core automotive business can maintain sufficient profitability and generate the cash required to fund new initiatives. In the near term, automotive margins, cash flow, and guidance for the fourth quarter could determine the market's reaction to the earnings release. Over the longer term, the company's valuation will increasingly depend on its ability to transform autonomous driving and artificial intelligence projects into scalable, revenue-generating businesses. The upcoming earnings report will therefore reveal not only the current state of Tesla's business, but also the strength of the financial foundations supporting its ambitious vision for the future.

data.title: XAU/USD Technical & Macro Outlook: October 2026
data.description:
Referenced assets

  • Hawkish Central Bank Expectations: Persistent inflationary pressures (with U.S. CPI at 3.7% in September) keep central banks hawkish, with market pricing leaning toward further Fed rate hikes or a “higher for longer” policy through early 2027.
  • Opposing Macro Forces on Gold: While high inflation provides safe-haven demand for gold, rising Treasury yields and a strong U.S. dollar from central bank tightening increase the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding bullion, creating downside pressure on gold.
  • Technical Bullish Flag Formation: Despite the recent price retreat from peaks near 5,600 within a descending channel, the technical structure views the move as a potential bullish flag pattern within the long-term uptrend since 2023, supported by key support between 4,000–4,120.

Macroeconomic Drivers & Central Bank Policy

Major central banks and economic bureaus are set to publish crucial inflation metrics in late October and early November 2026, including the European Central Bank and Bank of Japan monetary policy meetings on October 29–30, followed by the U.S. Consumer Price Index (CPI) release for October on November 10. Recent indicators show persistent inflationary pressure driven by sticky energy and shelter costs, with headline U.S. CPI rising to 3.7% year-over-year in September. These upcoming releases will reveal whether price pressures are structural or temporary, determining whether global headline inflation continues to hover well above the target 2% threshold in major economies.

In response, central banks—most notably the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC)—are maintaining a hawkish posture to rein in persistent inflation. Following a 25-basis-point rate hike to a target range of 3.75%–4.00% in September 2026, the FOMC enters its October 27–28 policy meeting under close market scrutiny as officials weigh additional tightening before year-end. If inflation data remain elevated, central banks will keep benchmark rates “higher for longer” or implement incremental rate hikes, thereby dampening economic expansion and cooling consumer demand.

These macroeconomic dynamics exert two opposing forces on gold prices. Higher inflation data initially boosts demand for gold as a traditional inflation hedge and safe-haven store of value. However, persistent inflation triggers hawkish rate responses from the FOMC, driving up real yields on U.S. Treasuries and strengthening the U.S. dollar, thereby increasing the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding bullion and pressuring prices downward. Ultimately, if upcoming CPI prints come in hotter than expected and prompt additional Fed rate hikes, gold is likely to experience short-term selling pressure; conversely, softer inflation data that signals an end to central bank tightening would provide strong tailwinds for a gold rally.

CME FedWatch Rate Expectations

According to CME FedWatch Tool pricing as of October 19, 2026, market expectations are overwhelmingly centered on additional Federal Reserve tightening through early 2027. For the upcoming October 28, 2026 meeting, markets reflect an 82.8% probability that the target rate will settle in the 375–400 bps range (indicating a hold at current levels) and a 17.2% chance of a hike to 400–425 bps. Heading into the final meeting of the year on December 9, 2026, sentiment shifts strongly toward a rate increase, with a 76.5% probability priced for a target range of 400–425 bps and a 15.5% probability placed on a further hike to 425–450 bps.

Looking ahead to the first policy meeting of 2027 on January 27, the market expects rates to remain elevated, with probabilities favoring either maintaining the 400–425 bps target (46.6%) or adjusting upward to the 425–450 bps band (42.1%).

XAU/USD weekly chart technical analysis and COT report updates

  • The price has been moving down within a well-defined descending channel (red trendlines) following a major peak near 5,600. So far, until proven otherwise, the descending channel can be considered a bullish flag formation for the initial long-term uptrend that began in early 2023 and is marked by the blue line.
  • Immediate support lies below price action, between the monthly S1 and the 2023 uptrend, in the 4000-4120 range. A second level of support falls at the annual pivot point of 3829.12.
  • An immediate confluence of resistance lies above price action, at the intersection of the fast EMA9 and the monthly pivot point of 4259.64. A second level of resistance falls near the monthly R1 of 4408.42, intersecting with the upper border of the flag formation.
  • Lagging momentum indicators, including the Relative Strength Index (RSI) and Stochastic Oscillator, remain constructively aligned with the underlying price action, tracking positively without exhibiting severe divergence.
  • The latest COT report released by the CFTC on Friday, October 16th, 2026, which includes data up to the end of day, Tuesday, October 13th, 2026, reflects that the most recent decline in gold price, which began in August of 2026, was accompanied by relatively unchanged open interest and declining volume. This suggests that the COT data did not support the price drop and a potential change in sentiment.

Conclusion

In summary, the outlook for XAU/USD remains framed by a tug-of-war between persistent hawkish central bank expectations and a constructively bullish long-term technical structure. While sustained inflationary pressure and market expectations of “higher for longer” Federal Reserve interest rates present ongoing macroeconomic headwinds—dampening bullion demand via elevated real yields and a strong U.S. dollar—the technical picture suggests that the recent price consolidation forms a bullish flag within a broader secular uptrend. A decisive breakout above immediate technical resistance around the 4,260–4,408 confluence region would signal a resumption of the broader rally, whereas a breakdown below primary support at 4,000–4,120 could expose lower pivot levels near 3,829.

data.title: Geopolitics, inflation and central banks set the direction for markets
data.description:
Referenced assets

  • A gradual recovery in Gulf oil supplies could bring prices lower during the winter, but the Strait of Hormuz remains a major source of risk.
  • China’s strong exports are offset by persistent weakness in its property sector and domestic demand.
  • US growth could reach around 2.4%-2,5% in 2026 and around 2.2-2,3% in 2027, supported in part by AI investment.
  • The Fed and ECB may keep policy restrictive as energy costs sustain inflation.
  • Bond yields could fall temporarily before fiscal pressures push them higher over the longer term.

Middle East tensions and oil prices

The situation in the Middle East remains a focus for investors, although tensions may gradually ease following the latest escalation. In recent months, growing volumes of oil from the Gulf region have been shipped through so-called “dark transits”, partly limiting the impact of disruptions to established export routes. Supplies could gradually return to normal during the winter, allowing oil prices to decline slowly.

The geopolitical premium is unlikely to disappear quickly, however. Markets remain highly sensitive to developments around the Strait of Hormuz, energy infrastructure and talks between the United States and Iran. Any delay in restoring normal flows could trigger another sharp rise in oil prices and bond yields.

China and the United States

The outlook for the world’s largest economies remains mixed. In China, strong exports are not enough to fully offset structural problems. Unresolved difficulties in construction and the property market continue to constrain domestic demand and business investment. The economy therefore remains heavily dependent on exports, leaving it more exposed to trade tensions and technology restrictions.

The US economy has proved relatively resilient to the effects of the war with Iran. Investment linked to artificial intelligence remains an important source of support, driving spending on data centres, semiconductors and energy infrastructure. US GDP could grow by 2.4% in 2026 and 2.3% in 2027.

Inflation remains a concern, staying well above the Federal Reserve’s target. A meaningful easing in price pressures may not come until the spring. The Fed responded to the increased inflation risk by raising interest rates by 25 basis points in September. One more increase is likely before the end of 2026, while the first and only cut may come as late as the end of 2027.

The euro area and the ECB

The euro area economy is holding up better than might have been expected given the high cost of energy. GDP could grow approximetly 1.0% in 2026 and little above 1% in 2027. At the same time, the energy shock is likely to keep inflation just below 3% both this year and next.

Against this backdrop, the European Central Bank is likely to raise its deposit rate by 25 basis points to 2.75% in December, then leave it unchanged until the end of 2027. The ECB will want to reduce the risk that elevated inflation expectations become entrenched, even if that comes at the expense of weaker economic activity.

Bond yields and the dollar

Over the medium and long term, the forces pushing bond yields higher still appear to dominate. Budget deficits remain too large in many Western countries, while growing political fragmentation makes fiscal consolidation harder. Investors may therefore continue to demand a higher premium to finance government debt.

A temporary calm in bond markets is possible before next spring. Current prices may reflect too many expected rate increases from both the Fed and the ECB. If energy prices begin to fall and inflation stops rising, some of those expectations could be revised. That would allow yields to decline for a time and could improve sentiment in equity markets.

In the coming quarters, the dollar may come under pressure from attempts by Donald Trump’s administration to limit the Federal Reserve’s independence, as well as its aggressive approach to trading partners. More countries may consequently look for alternatives to the US currency. This would be a slow process, but it could support the euro against the dollar over the longer term.

data.title: Cryptos pulled back but sentiment rebounds, Opportunity? – BTC and Ethereum (ETH) Technical Outlook
data.description:
Referenced assets

  • Bitcoin retraced from the $80,000 level, along with other altcoins, and they are lagging the US Equities after the latest US-Iran peace draft
  • Cryptos have been consolidating for a while, but present interesting technical indications – A trap or an opportunity?
  • Exploring a Technical Analysis and trading levels for Bitcoin and Ethereum

Bitcoin has pulled back from the important $80,000 level, and this drop has also affected the wider altcoin market.

Right now, cryptocurrencies are somewhat falling behind US stocks after the recent US-Iran peace draft. Nasdaq, normally highly correlated to digital assets, has quickly moved back toward new highs thanks to optimism about diplomacy, but despite the correlations, cryptocurrencies have barely moved.

This clear difference shows that digital assets are not following the usual trends in the broader market, at least for now.

Cryptocurrencies have been stuck in a long period of relative sideways movement, unable to break out as some traders hoped.

This may have been frustrating for those looking for quick gains, but there are still some interesting technical signals to watch. The big question now is whether this slow price action is a warning sign or a chance to buy at a discount.

The digital asset market has shown resilience by bouncing off important moving averages, even though there has not been a big surge in retail trading.

If overall market sentiment remains positive and the peace talks continue to hold, Bitcoin and other cryptocurrencies could soon rally and make up for lost ground compared to tech stocks – But this will depend on if investors can remain hopeful about the deal and its effect.

Let's dive right into a technical analysis and key trading levels for both Bitcoin and Ethereum to spot if a clear breakout in indeed into play from here.

  • Stock Markets stall, too early for the deal ? Dow Jones, Nasdaq and S&P 500 Intraday Levels
  • The deal is still quite unsure, Crude Oil back above $100 – WTI Technical analysis

Bitcoin has broken its recent upward channel that brought the action above $80,000, but lookign at current trading, the action is far from bearish.

The pullback stalled right at the 4H 200-period MA ($77,000) and is currently acting as support.

Bouncing back above $78,800, the 4H 50 MA, opens the way for a new test of a higher break.

On the other hand, bears will want to see a break of the 200 MA with an extension below $75,000.

data.title: France: Debt risks are mounting
data.description:
Referenced assets

  • A narrower French bond spread has eased immediate market stress, but fiscal concerns remain unresolved.
  • High public debt leaves euro area governments vulnerable to rising borrowing costs.
  • Pressure on Italian bonds highlights the risk of tensions spreading beyond France.
  • Stronger banks and ECB intervention tools provide greater protection than during the previous debt crisis.
  • Credible fiscal reforms remain essential to restoring investor confidence.

Temporary relief offers no lasting solution

French government bonds remain under pressure as investors question the sustainability of public finances. The spread between French and German ten-year yields narrowed from almost 150 to around 140 basis points, but the improvement did not remove the underlying risks.

Marine Le Pen’s pledge to reduce the budget deficit substantially if she wins the election helped calm markets. Investors will nevertheless focus on whether those commitments can be implemented, particularly given political and public resistance to spending cuts or tax increases.

High debt revives familiar concerns

The situation shares several features with the euro area sovereign debt crisis of more than a decade ago. Public debt remains elevated, and debt-to-GDP ratios in several major economies exceed their levels before that crisis.

Across the euro area, government debt averages around 90% of GDP, compared with approximately 80% in 2009 and the EU treaty threshold of 60%. Such debt burdens make public finances more sensitive to higher borrowing costs, especially when economic growth is too weak to support a sustained reduction in debt ratios.

Contagion risks extend beyond France

Rising risk premiums on Italian bonds suggest that investors’ concerns are spreading. The scale of these moves remains considerably smaller than during the previous sovereign debt crisis, but the mechanism is familiar: higher financing costs weaken the fiscal outlook, prompting investors to demand still higher yields.

France’s economic size and the scale of its sovereign bond market make it particularly significant for the monetary union. A prolonged loss of confidence could therefore have wider consequences than stress in a smaller economy.

Political resistance complicates adjustment

A lasting reduction in the deficit would require difficult decisions on spending, taxation or both. Without sufficient political support, ambitious fiscal targets may fail to restore confidence.

Markets will consequently judge the substance and feasibility of budget measures rather than promises alone. Delays in implementing reforms could keep borrowing costs elevated and make debt stabilisation harder.

Stronger safeguards reduce crisis risks

The euro area is better equipped to withstand financial stress than it was during the previous crisis. France has a developed economy, functioning institutions and a broad tax base. European banks are also better capitalised, reducing the risk that sovereign bond losses rapidly develop into a banking crisis requiring costly government support.

The ECB’s Outright Monetary Transactions programme and Transmission Protection Instrument provide additional safeguards. Both allow intervention in bond markets under specified conditions and can help contain destabilising selling pressure. However, neither replaces credible fiscal policy, and support should not be regarded as automatic.

Fiscal credibility remains decisive

A renewed, full-scale sovereign debt crisis need not be the baseline scenario. A prolonged period of volatility and elevated French borrowing costs may be more likely.

Nevertheless, the longer France lacks a convincing plan to stabilise public debt, the greater the risk that tensions spread to other euro area economies. Institutional safeguards can limit market disruption, but a durable recovery in confidence ultimately depends on credible fiscal action.

The outlook for the stock market in France

These fiscal concerns are also reflected in France’s equity market, with the CAC 40 falling sharply in recent weeks. Uncertainty over debt sustainability and the feasibility of deficit reduction is weighing on investor confidence. Banking stocks are particularly exposed, as pressure on sovereign bonds can weaken balance sheets and raise funding costs.

The chart shows the CAC 40 retreating sharply from its recent peak near 8,750 points and testing the lower boundary of its rising channel. The next key support lies around 7,500 points, with a break below it potentially opening the way towards 6,750. For now, the decline remains within the broader upward trend, although the latest sell-off has weakened the technical outlook.

data.title: The US labour market is losing momentum – as is the USD
data.description:
Referenced assets

  • The U.S. labor market is losing momentum, but not collapsing. Nonfarm payrolls rose by only 57,000, previous months were revised lower, and hiring has clearly slowed, while layoffs remain limited.
  • The drop in unemployment is less positive than it looks. The unemployment rate fell to 4.2%, but this was partly due to a decline in labor force participation to 61.5%, meaning some people stopped actively looking for work.
  • The report reduced pressure on the Fed to tighten policy further. Slower job growth and easing wage pressure revived hopes for future rate cuts, weakened the dollar, and supported assets such as gold, Bitcoin, and EUR/USD.

June data from the U.S. labor market showed a clear weakening in employment momentum. Nonfarm payrolls increased by only 57,000, significantly below economists’ expectations. In addition, data for the previous two months were revised downward, weakening earlier signals that had suggested greater resilience in the labor market.

At first glance, the decline in the unemployment rate to 4.2% appeared positive. However, this is not an unambiguous sign of improvement. The drop in unemployment was accompanied by a marked decline in labor force participation. The participation rate fell to 61.5%, reaching its lowest level in more than five years. This means that some individuals stopped actively looking for work and were therefore no longer included in unemployment statistics.

Companies are not conducting mass layoffs, but they are hiring more cautiously

The report does not point to a labor market collapse, but it does show increasing caution among employers. Initial jobless claims remained almost unchanged, suggesting that the scale of layoffs remains limited. The issue, therefore, is not a sharp reduction in employment, but a weaker willingness among companies to create new jobs.

The largest decline in employment was recorded in the leisure and hospitality sector. This is particularly important because, at this time of year, the industry typically increases seasonal hiring. Weaker-than-usual employment growth may indicate a more cautious approach by companies toward consumer demand and future operating costs.

At the same time, some sectors continued to support the labor market. Healthcare and social assistance remained the main source of employment growth. Job numbers also increased in manufacturing and construction. Weakness persisted, however, in the information sector, where employment declined for the seventeenth time in the past eighteen months.

Wages are rising, but inflationary pressure is easing

Average hourly earnings rose by 3.5% year over year in June. This increase shows that wages are still growing, but they are no longer generating inflationary pressure as strong as during the period of peak labor market tightness. For the Federal Reserve, this may be an argument that employment conditions remain relatively stable and do not require an abrupt policy response.

From the perspective of households, however, the picture is less favorable. Slower employment growth means fewer opportunities to find a new job, while inflation continues to limit the real purchasing power of wages. Even if nominal wages are rising, many workers may not feel a clear improvement in their financial situation.

Markets took note of the report’s weakness

The release triggered a moderately positive reaction in financial markets. The S&P 500 opened higher, while U.S. Treasury yields declined. Investors scaled back expectations for further interest rate hikes by the Fed, although they still priced in at least one rate increase this year.

The market reaction shows that weaker employment data were interpreted as a factor reducing pressure on the central bank. If the labor market continues to lose momentum, the Fed may have fewer reasons to tighten monetary policy further.

A mixed picture of the U.S. economy

The data were disappointing, but they should not fundamentally change the overall assessment of the economy. The labor market reflects uneven economic growth, in which some sectors are still creating jobs while others are clearly slowing. From the Fed’s perspective, the situation does not look alarming, as the labor market is not generating additional inflationary pressure. For American households, however, it means more difficult conditions, especially when limited employment opportunities coincide with persistently high living costs.

Kevin Warsh’s first press conference as FOMC Chair was perceived as hawkish and fueled concerns about an interest rate hike in the United States. As a result, the dollar strengthened significantly in recent weeks. Following today’s NFP report, hopes for an interest rate cut have resurfaced. Of course, with core PCE inflation currently at 3.4% year over year, this remains unlikely. Nevertheless, today’s reading creates a balance between arguments for monetary easing and monetary tightening, given the Fed’s dual mandate of maximum employment and price stability. It was precisely these hopes that led to a weakening of the dollar. EUR/USD is currently trading at 1.1446, up 0.59%. Instruments quoted in USD, which have recently failed to generate returns for investors, also deserve attention. Gold is up 2.37% today, while Bitcoin has gained 2.64%.

A labor market without collapse, but also without strength

The June report shows that the U.S. labor market is in a phase of clear slowdown. There are no signs of mass layoffs or a sharp deterioration in conditions, but it is becoming increasingly difficult to describe the market as strong. Companies are acting cautiously, new jobs are being created more slowly, and the decline in unemployment is partly the result of lower labor force participation.

The key takeaway from the report is therefore that the labor market is not collapsing, but it is losing resilience. For the Fed, this means less pressure from wages and employment, while for workers it means more challenging job-search conditions and limited improvement in real incomes.

data.title: Bitcoin Deepens Losses - Crypto Market Under Pressure
data.description:
Referenced assets

  • Bitcoin is under strong selling pressure, falling over 17% in a week and dropping below USD 60,000. The decline was intensified by USD 532 million in long liquidations on Binance, which triggered additional forced selling.
  • Market sentiment worsened after Strategy sold part of its bitcoin holdings. Although the sale was small — 32 BTC for USD 2.5 million — it raised concerns that the largest corporate bitcoin holder could make further sales in the future.
  • The broader crypto market is weak due to macro and demand concerns. Strong U.S. labor data reduced hopes for rate cuts, retail investors are shifting toward AI-related tech stocks, ETF inflows remain too small to support prices, and security concerns after the Zcash vulnerability further damaged trust.

Bitcoin has come under heavy selling pressure and has already lost more than 17 percent since the beginning of the week. On Friday, its price fell below the psychological barrier of USD 60,000, increasing investor concerns about a further deepening of the correction. Bitcoin has fallen below its 200-week SMA for the first time in three years. From its all-time high near USD 126,000, the leading cryptocurrency has already lost more than half of its value.

Long liquidations increase pressure on the market

The scale of the declines was amplified by the forced closure of leveraged positions. Over the past 24 hours, long positions worth USD 532 million were liquidated on the Binance exchange. Such a large wave of liquidations shows that many investors betting on a bitcoin rebound were forced to close their positions, which further increased selling pressure in the market.

This mechanism often deepens declines, as automatic liquidations lead to further sell orders. As a result, the market can move more sharply than would be implied solely by incoming macroeconomic data or the decisions of the largest investors.

Strategy’s Bitcoin sale weighed on sentiment

One of the factors worsening sentiment was the news that Strategy, the largest corporate holder of bitcoin and a company associated with Michael Saylor, had sold part of its bitcoin holdings. The company sold 32 bitcoins for USD 2.5 million. Although the transaction was small compared with the company’s overall portfolio, it carried significant symbolic weight.

It was only Strategy’s second bitcoin sale since it began making purchases in 2020. The company explained the decision as necessary to pay coupons to holders of preferred shares, but investors interpreted it as a possible weakening of the long-standing narrative of holding bitcoin indefinitely.

The market is primarily concerned that this small sale could foreshadow further, larger transactions in the future. This risk was highlighted by Peter Schiff, a well-known bitcoin critic, who stressed that the problem is not the scale of the current sale itself, but its potential consequences for investor confidence. Before this transaction, Strategy had reportedly purchased a total of 843,738 BTC for nearly USD 64 billion, which is why any change in the company’s strategy is being closely watched by the market.

Declines spread across the entire cryptocurrency market

Selling pressure was not limited to bitcoin. Ethereum fell by around 23 percent over the week to USD 1,555, while Solana lost about 22 percent, dropping to USD 63.75. Weakness was also visible in shares of companies linked to cryptocurrencies. Strategy’s stock fell by almost 10 percent, while Coinbase shares declined by 8.4 percent.

A modest positive signal came from inflows into U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs yesterday after 13 days of outflows. However, the scale of these inflows, amounting to just over USD 3 million, was too small to change the overall market picture. In practice, this means that institutional demand remains too weak to effectively stop the current sell-off.

Strong U.S. Data reduces hopes for rate cuts

Sentiment was also hurt by strong data from the U.S. labor market. Nonfarm payrolls rose by 172,000 in May, clearly above expectations. Such data reduces the likelihood of swift interest rate cuts in the United States, which is unfavorable for risk assets, including cryptocurrencies.

The strong labor market report weakened the narrative of imminent monetary policy easing, while bitcoin currently lacks a clear macroeconomic catalyst that could support a rebound.

Retail investors shift their attention to tech stocks

An additional problem for the crypto market is the outflow of some retail investors toward technology stocks, especially companies linked to artificial intelligence. Retail investors have largely left the cryptocurrency market and returned to equities, making it difficult to identify new sources of demand for bitcoin.

In an environment of weakening interest and a lack of fresh capital, every negative piece of news can trigger a stronger price reaction. This applies both to macroeconomic data and to decisions by major entities holding significant bitcoin reserves.

Security issues weaken trust in Crypto

The cryptocurrency market is also struggling with concerns over trust in the security of blockchain technology. Investors paid particular attention to a vulnerability in the Zcash network, after which the cryptocurrency’s price fell by more than 40 percent in a single day. Developers fixed the bug, but they were unable to clearly determine whether it had been exploited to create additional tokens.

This situation increased concerns that increasingly advanced artificial intelligence models may in the future help detect similar vulnerabilities in other cryptocurrency projects. For a market already under downward pressure, such information further worsens sentiment.

Lack of new sources of demand makes a rebound difficult

The current sell-off in bitcoin is the result of several negative factors overlapping: strong U.S. economic data, reduced expectations for interest rate cuts, investors shifting toward technology stocks, concerns about Strategy’s future actions, trust issues related to the security of some crypto projects, and the large scale of long liquidations in the leveraged instruments market.

Bitcoin remains under pressure, and the lack of clear new sources of demand means that a quick and sustained rebound may be difficult. The market appears weakened, and investors are watching increasingly closely to see whether the drop below USD 60,000 proves to be only a brief breach of an important level or a continuation of the downward trend that began in October 2025.

data.title: Chart alert: Bitcoin (BTC/USD) potential near-term bullish reversal emerging from the sub-$70K plunge
data.description:
Referenced assets

Key takeaways

  • Bitcoin plunged 16% over the past two weeks and briefly fell below the US$70,000 psychological level after MicroStrategy’s partial Bitcoin sale shattered the long-standing “never sell” narrative that had supported market sentiment.
  • Despite the sharp decline, several contrarian indicators suggest selling pressure may be nearing exhaustion, including an extremely oversold daily RSI reading, a surge in long-position liquidations, and signs of renewed accumulation by long-term holders.
  • Technical and on-chain metrics indicate the potential for a near-term bullish reversal above the key US$62,250 support level, with upside targets at US$74,880 and US$82,815 if buying momentum returns.

Let’s unpack the primary drivers and the technical setup.

The plunge and its fundamental catalysts

On Monday and Tuesday (1–2 June 2026), the cryptocurrency market absorbed a significant psychological blow. Spot BTC/USD tumbled sharply, slipping below the $70,000 psychological threshold and falling 16% over the past two weeks. It printed an intraday low of $65,370 on Wednesday, 3 June 2026.

The dominant driver of this week’s movement was the revelation that MicroStrategy, the world’s largest corporate holder of Bitcoin, sold a portion of its holdings for the first time in four years.

While the market impact is less about the absolute volume of the sale and more about the erosion of consensus, it effectively shattered founder Michael Saylor’s widely echoed “never sell” iron law.

This pivot disrupted the pricing anchor the market had historically relied on, injecting uncertainty and triggering a wave of defensive selling.

Technical and on-chain analysis suggesting a setup for a bullish reversal

The 16% plunge in BTC/USD has left it hovering just above its $62,250 key medium-term pivotal support and the lower boundary of its long-term secular ascending channel running from the December 2018 low.

In addition, the daily RSI momentum indicator hit a significant oversold level of 21.8 on Tuesday, 2 June 2026, its lowest since 5 February 2026, triggering a 35% rally in BTC/USD over the next three months.

Secondly, utilising TradingView’s crypto derivatives indicators for crypto futures and perpetual swaps, such as from Bybit, Binance, and OKX.

Aggregated long liquidation data (derived from various exchanges) spiked to $482 million on Tuesday, 2 June 2026, indicating that many leveraged long positions in Bitcoin futures and perpetual swaps were forced closed due to margin calls.

A similar rise in long liquidations ($481 million) also occurred on 5 February 2026, when capitulation led to a 35% rally in BTC/USD.

Thirdly, on-chain indicator: the percentage of 1-year active supply for Bitcoin has declined steadily over the past three weeks, from 40.3% on 23 April 2026 to 39.3% on Wednesday, 3 June 2026, at the time of writing.

Active supply 1-year measures the total number of unique cryptocurrency units that have moved at least once over the past 1 year. This metric tracks the portion of supply that has been involved in on-chain transactions during the trailing 365-day period.

A decreasing active supply often signals accumulation by long-term holders, a bullish condition for Bitcoin in the current context.

Hence, based on these factors, BTC/USD is now ripe for a potential near-term bullish reversal above the $62,250 key medium-term support, with intermediate resistance at $74,880. A clearance above it would signal a retest of the $82,815 medium-term resistance (also close to the 200-day moving average).

On the other hand, a daily close below $62,250 invalidates the recovery scenario and extends the corrective decline towards the $57,590/52,590 long-term pivotal support zone.
